subject: Post-call: RAG eval & next steps / recommended models & reranker
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RAG eval & next steps

Thanks for your time today, Jordan — quick recap + proposed next steps from our RAG discussion. Appreciate Aisha joining as well.

Call highlights:
- Goal: improve answer grounding for product docs + support KB (reduce hallucination, increase precision@1 for top answer).
- Current infra: hybrid DB + keyword search; want to move to vector-first retrieval with a lightweight rerank stage.
- Success criteria discussed: precision@1 >= 0.75 on customer QA set; grounding rate (answers citing source) > 85%; end-to-end latency target for a single-query lookup + model generation under 600ms p50 (where feasible).

Quick recommendations (model + retrieval):
1) Model choices (quality / cost tradeoffs):
   - Redwood-Chat-13B (best quality for finetuned conversational outputs)
   - Llama-2-13B-chat (good quality, lower cost when quantized)
   - Redwood-Instruct-7B-4bit (recommended for high throughput testing; good baseline)

2) Embedding / vector config:
   - Embedding model: redwood/embed-large-v1 (or text-embedding-3-large equivalent)
   - Vector store: Milvus or Faiss on dedicated nodes; index type IVF-PQ (if using Faiss) or HNSW for fast recall
   - Retrieval: initial candidate top_k = 100, then rerank top_k_rerank = 20

3) Reranker recommendation:
   - Cross-encoder reranker (e.g., cross-encoder-roberta-large-msmarco) for quality-sensitive workloads
   - For lower-cost option, lightweight lexical BM25 pass followed by a small bi-encoder rescoring model

4) Evaluation plan / metrics to capture:
   - Precision@1, Precision@3, MRR; grounding ratio (% answers that cite a source); hallucination rate (manual label)
   - A blind human eval: 200-300 queries, 3 raters, binary relevance + grounding label

Attachments and artifacts I've included:
- acme_rag_benchmark_report_v1.pdf (initial benchmark we ran on a 150-query set)
- acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (seed prompts we used during the call)
- mutual_action_plan.xlsx (timeline & owners)

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi / Dev: run the 250-query blind eval using Redwood-Chat-13B and Redwood-Instruct-7B variants (Milvus + cross-encoder reranker).
- I will share the full prompt set + benchmark link (attached) and schedule a 30min checkpoint next week to review results.
- Jordan/Aisha: please confirm whether the security contact (infosec) should be looped in for any data movement questions — we won't move PHI but want to ensure compliance posture is clear.

Proposed times: Tue Jul 1, 10:00am PT for a follow-up (30m).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Jordan — great questions. Short answers + config we recommend for the blind eval below.

Reranker threshold: we typically use a cross-encoder normalized score threshold ~0.7 for auto-suppression in production (this is model-dependent; we'll calibrate).

Minimum queries: 250 gives us stable signal for precision@1 with 3 raters; you can run 200 as a smaller smoke test but expect wider confidence intervals.

Recommended eval config (concrete):
- Embedding model: redwood/embed-large-v1 (384/1024 dims depending on model)
- Vector index: Milvus managed cluster (HNSW for recall-heavy, or IVF-PQ for large corpora)
- Candidate retrieval: top_k_candidates = 100
- Rerank stage: cross-encoder reranker on top_k_rerank = 20; normalized score in [0,1]
- Auto-suppression threshold: 0.7 (initial); fallback: show "I don't know" template when below threshold
- Generation model (for eval): Redwood-Chat-13B for quality baseline; Redwood-Instruct-7B-4bit for throughput baseline

Grounding & quality metrics to capture during the run:
- Precision@1, Precision@3, MRR (automated)
- Grounding ratio (human label: does the model cite a correct source?)
- Hallucination rate (human label) — track by error type
- Latency (retrieval + generation) p50/p95

Benchmark doc & prompt sets are attached and available at the link below:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/benchmark-report

Plan:
- Rishi will run the 250-query blind eval across the two model variants and the reranker configuration described above.
- Dev: please provision a Milvus index with the current KB dump and export a sample of the top-100 retrievals for the first 250 queries (we'll need those for labeling).
- I will coordinate the labeling instructions and share the labeling sheet + rubric.

Proposed follow-up: Tue Jul 1, 10:00am PT (I'll send the calendar invite).
